top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, Ormco, Spark, KLOwen, Lightforce, Angel, suresmile, clearcorrect, Invisalign, self-ligating braces, twin brackets, SmartSTL
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, time saving, visit reduction, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, efficiency in bracket systems, rentability, adaptive aligner change, average visit reduction, efficiency in second and third order movements
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM will actually reduce chair time, appointments, or costs, and want proof that it improves efficiency or profitability compared to their current workflow. Some question whether the investment in DM is justified by measurable practice gains.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, white paper, peer-reviewed, recent studies, only Australian studies, only German studies, only academic publication, no format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
Are Damon brackets more efficient than other brands?
Reduced chair time, recent studies, practice efficiencies for aligners
top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct comparative studies quantifying ROI and efficiency gains for specific appliances and geographies are limited. More robust, region-specific economic analyses and real-world practice workflow data are needed.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI and SmartSTL for clinical monitoring and diagnosis
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of SmartSTL, occlusal assessment, class I goal, accuracy of scanning, AI efficiency, predictability, FDA class I, accuracy with aligner unseats
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM’s AI and SmartSTL are accurate enough for clinical decision-making, especially compared to in-person or intraoral scans. Some are concerned about false positives/negatives or regulatory validation.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, white paper, clinical study, peer-reviewed, no format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
How accurate is DentalMonitorings AI and will it save me money
Looking for white papers on Smart STL accuracy to help convince a doctor to use it in the practice.
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application
How accurate is SmartSTL AI
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for more peer-reviewed, head-to-head accuracy studies (especially for SmartSTL) and regulatory validation data. Evidence comparing AI/SmartSTL to gold-standard clinical assessments is especially valued.
